title: Hawaiian Airlines and Made in Hawaiʻi Festival: More than 30 years of supporting local businesses
summary: Hawaiian Airlines is celebrating more than 30 years of partnership with the Made in Hawaiʻi Festival, supporting local artisans, entrepreneurs and small businesses across the Islands.
body_markdown:
More than 80 Hawaiian Airlines employee volunteers welcomed festivalgoers to its Island Style Mākeke, a space inspired by the familiar character of Hawaiʻi’s farm stands and community markets. Hawaiian shared the space with NOHO Home and Mana Up, highlighting products created through local partnerships. NOHO Home introduced exclusive colorways from its co-branded Leihōkū Collection, while Mana Up featured Hawaiian Airlines collaborations created with Nick Kuchar, Paper Crane Soaps, Lex Breezy, Lahaʻole, Lola Pilar and AVVA.


This year’s festival also opened with its first VIP Access Night, presented by[Huakaʻi by Hawaiian](https://www.hawaiianairlines.com/content/huakai) , the carrier’s free travel benefits program exclusively for kamaʻāina (Hawaiʻi residents). Huakaʻi members received early access to tickets and special offers for the festival. All 7,000 VIP attendees received an exclusive cooler tote, featuring artwork by local artist Lola Pilar upon entering,


Hawaiian Airline’s commitment to culinary talent shined with live chef demonstrations inspired by its inflight menus. On Saturday, Chef Dell Valdez, who has helped shape Hawaiian’s international menus, prepared ʻulu spezzatino with Kahuku corn polenta. On Sunday, Hawaiian Airlines Chef Sheldon Simeon, who created the carrier’s recent pre-order offerings for its Main Cabin guests, demonstrated his fried garlic noodles and signed copies of his newest cookbook, “Ohana Style: Food from Hawai‘i, for Your Family,” for festivalgoers.
